verdict.rationale: Lithic documents dedicated sandbox endpoints that simulate transaction events from a merchant acquirer, and explicitly documents simulating authorization requests, so ASA and auth-rule logic can be tested before live traffic. The evidence only names authorization simulation; the other lifecycle stages the story lists are covered at most by the general 'transaction events' and 'end-to-end' wording. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of clearing, reversal, refund and decline simulation endpoints, and hands-on or independent corroboration of full-lifecycle sandbox testing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can simulate the whole transaction lifecycle in the sandbox — authorizations, clearings, reversals, refunds, and declines — so my auth logic is tested before a real card ever swipes

citations.quote: The sandbox environment has additional endpoints to simulate transaction events originating from a merchant acquirer.
Simulate an authorization request from the payment network as if it came from a merchant acquirer.
A safe environment mirroring production — run cards, transactions, and webhooks end-to-end.
